title: Offline conformance fixture
description: Executable spec for the boot of an app with offline support (static flows). Every Orca SDK (Flutter, Swift, Kotlin) runs each case the same way: seed the store with `saved`, answer GET /version with `version` and GET /config with `config` (recording the requests in order), run the SDK's preload (Flutter: `OrcaApp.preload` over a `StaticFlowManager`), let its saves land, then compare `expected`: the requests, the result, the store after, and, when the boot gave a config, what the page cache serves for each path once the dynamic paths of that config are known. The Flutter SDK is the oracle: an expected value is what it does.

Case.description: One cold start: a fresh cache over the store as `saved` leaves it, as after a restart.

description.description: What the case pins, with the row it belongs to; a Flutter quirk kept on purpose says so here.

version.description: The answer to GET /api/v1/app/:appId/version, or "fail": the request does not reach the server (no network). On 200 the body is the engine's getVersionInfo (core/app.ts): `{flows: {name: version}}`, every flow listed, 0 for a flow without a version, plus `forceUpdate: true` only when the app sets it.

config.description: The answer to GET /api/v1/app/:appId/config, present when the case requests it. On 200 the body is a /config body as the engine serves it (core/app.ts getNavConfig; the shape of navigation-fixture.schema.json#/definitions/Config): a flow's `version` is left out when it is 0; a static flow carries `isStatic` and `pages`, its non-dynamic pages pre-rendered and keyed by route path with no leading slash; a dynamic route carries `isDynamic` and has no page. A request to /config in a case without this key is a transport failure.

Answer.description: An HTTP answer. The runner sends `body` as its JSON text with status `status`.

SavedStore.description: The store before the boot, by Flutter's key names (StaticFlowManager). Each value is written here as JSON; the store holds its JSON text. An absent key is not in the store.

orca_nav_config.description: The raw /config body saved by an earlier online boot.

^orca_pages_.+$.description: orca_pages_<flow>: the saved pages of one static flow, keyed by route path with no leading slash.

Versions.description: Flow name to version. Only flows whose /config entry has a version are saved.

requests.description: The requests the boot made, in order.

oneOf.description: A config: its flows, by name, with the version each carries (null when the entry has none). Whether it is the saved config or the fetched one follows from `requests`.
/version said forceUpdate: the host shows its force-update screen.

The boot fails. A string is preload's own message, exact (Flutter throws Exception(message)). `{status}` is the client's error for a /config answer with that status, passed through unchanged (Flutter: OrcaClientException.statusCode).

saved.description: The store after the boot, once its saves have landed. Its keys are exactly the keys in the store.

orca_nav_config.description: "config": the exact body text this case's /config answer was sent with. "saved": the text the case started with, unchanged.

^orca_pages_.+$.description: The set of page paths stored for that flow (not the page JSON, so no SDK has to re-encode pages byte for byte).

serves.description: Path (route path, no leading slash) to the pageId the page cache returns for it after the boot, or null when the page goes to the network (a dynamic route, a path no static flow of the config saved). Empty when the result is not a config.
